authoredBy: P1.2c — generic story bible schema, Republic as second test fixture

world.era: Classical Athens, ~380 BC — Plato's dialogues staged after the fall of the Thirty Tyrants
world.setting: A two-host deep dive into Plato's Republic: the Piraeus harbor walk (agora), the cave of shadows (cave), the ship of state (shipDeck), Cephalus's house (colonnade), the manuscript page (manuscript), and the Athenian street (street).

narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.look: The second voice of the deep dive: dark blazer, open collar, probing questions about justice and the ideal city.

plato.name: Plato
plato.look: Classical Athenian philosopher in draped himation robe, dignified beard, author of The Republic.

socrates.name: Socrates
socrates.look: Elderly barefoot Athenian philosopher, inquisitive and humble in plain himation.

glaucon.name: Glaucon
glaucon.look: Young Athenian aristocrat in crimson chlamys cloak, ambitious interlocutor.

thrasymachus.name: Thrasymachus
thrasymachus.look: Cynical sophist: barrel-chested, loud toga, aggressive posture, believes justice is the interest of the stronger.

everyman.name: The Citizen
everyman.look: Generic Athenian citizen standing in for the audience: simple chiton, observing the dialogue.

manuscript.look: The lecture table: papyrus-grain field where the hosts dissect the Republic's arguments.

shipDeck.look: The Ship of State allegory: a wooden vessel deck under uncertain sky, the captain and the sailors.

cave.look: Plato's cave: chained prisoners facing a wall of dancing shadows, firelight behind them.

colonnade.look: Cephalus's house: a shaded marble colonnade where the dialogue begins over the Bendis festival.

street.look: Athenian street: dust, low walls, the walk down to the Piraeus harbor.

agora.look: The Athenian agora: open public square with stoa columns, citizens debating under open sky.

sky.look: The open Mediterranean sky: the Form of the Good as the sun illuminating all things.

stage.look: The theatrical stage: where the Republic's thought experiments play out as staged scenarios.

horizon.look: The distant horizon beyond Athens: the line between the visible world and the intelligible realm.

spine.claim: The walk to Piraeus — what is justice? Cephalus, Polemarchus, Thrasymachus challenge Socrates.
Building Kallipolis — guardians, auxiliaries, producers; the tripartite soul mirrors the tripartite city.
The philosopher-king, the cave allegory, the divided line — knowledge vs. opinion.
Five regimes decay: aristocracy to tyranny; the tyrant's soul is the most miserable.
The Allegory of Er, the Allegory of the Cave revisited — choose the just life.
